subject: DPA: Clarifying cross-border access for snapshots and retention language
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@atlas-payments.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Payments Legal <legal@atlas-payments.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines — snapshot/backups & cross-border access

Sofia,

Thanks for the call earlier — attaching our latest redlines (Atlas_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx). Two items we need clarity on before we can move to legal sign-off:

1) Snapshot/backups: your redline currently allows "access by support and engineering personnel, as necessary," without geographic limits. We need a written assurance that snapshot restores or engineer access for Atlas customer data will not be performed from outside the US/EU without prior notice and contractual approval.

2) Retention of snapshots: your table lists "snapshot retention: 90 days" but the DPA's backup carve-out in section 4 allows longer-term cold backups. Please clarify the maximum retention for recoverable snapshots vs immutable archival backups and what proof-of-deletion will look like for each.

Proposed ask: add a one-sentence residency constraint for restore/access and include an appendix describing retention windows by storage tier.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) commit to US-only engineer restore access for Atlas tenant data by default, and (b) provide a monthly deletion ledger for snapshot lifecycle events?

We will also need SOC 2 artifacts and a brief description of the playbook for discovery/legal holds if a regulatory subpoena arrives.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Privacy & Contracts
Atlas Payments

Attachments: Atlas_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx (redline), snapshot-retention-examples.csv (sample)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — snapshot/backups & cross-border access

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the redline doc. Quick answers up front, with proposed contractual language below:

(a) Default engineer restore/access locality: yes — Redwood can commit that routine restore activity for Atlas tenant data is restricted to personnel operating from the US by default. We will include the following proposed clause to the DPA under "Data Access and Locality":

"For customer accounts electing US residency, Redwood will ensure that, by default, engineer-initiated access to live snapshots, temporary restores, and interactive debugging sessions for Atlas Payment customer data is performed by personnel located in the United States unless Atlas provides prior written consent for access from other jurisdictions."

(b) Snapshot retention vs archival: we differentiate 'recoverable snapshots' (hot/warm tier) and 'archival backups' (cold tier). Proposed commitments: recoverable snapshots retained up to 30 days; warm-tier rollups retained up to 90 days for selected workloads (mutually agreed); archival backups retained for up to 12 months unless otherwise contractually specified. Proof-of-deletion: we can provide a monthly ledger containing timestamped lifecycle events (created, truncated, expired, deleted) for recoverable snapshots.

I attached a short CSV with examples (snapshot-retention-examples.csv).

Next steps: Marissa and Ben — can you review the wording below for legal/ops feasibility and let Atlas know if there are any absolute blockers?

Thanks,
Sofia
Head, Infosec Partnerships (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: snapshot-retention-examples.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — snapshot/backups & cross-border access

Sofia / team — technical context and constraints below. TL;DR: US-only engineer access for restores is operationally feasible with standard controls, but there are some edge cases to call out (disaster recovery, failover, and QA restore).

Points:
- Recoverable snapshots (hot/warm): these are on SSD pools attached to serving clusters and are accessible for fast restores. 30 days default retention is straightforward.
- Warm-tier 90 days: acceptable if Atlas agrees to selective workload scope; more retained snapshots increases storage and snapshot restore surface area for compliance.
- Archive backups: tape/colder object storage replication may be kept for 12 months; physical location depends on replication policy (we can pin to US region for Atlas).
- Edge case: DR failover — if a regional outage requires engineers in another region to perform an emergency restore, we can commit to immediate written notice to Atlas plus after-action report; we cannot guarantee absolutely that a remote engineer won't be involved during cross-region DR unless Atlas wants explicit contractual prohibition (which may degrade recovery RTO).

Operational controls we suggest included in the DPA or an appendix:
- Dedicated access groups for Atlas restores (role-based access; break-glass workflow).
- IP allow-listing for restore consoles tied to Atlas security ops.
- Monthly deletion ledger (automated export) + quarterly retention reviews.

No blockers from infra; needs legal text to be precise about DR exception handling.

—Ben
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@atlas-payments.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — snapshot/backups & cross-border access

Elena / Daniel — appreciate the asks. From a contracting perspective we can accept the US-only default for engineer-initiated restores and provide the monthly deletion ledger as described, subject to one clarifying change and a DR carve-out:

1) Change: replace blanket "no access from outside the US" language with the following mutually agreed wording to preserve recoverability: 

"Redwood will by default limit engineer-initiated access for Atlas-resident data to personnel operating from the United States. In the event of a bona fide regional disaster recovery event, Redwood may temporarily engage personnel outside the United States to restore service, provided Redwood (i) issues prior notice to Atlas where practicable or (ii) provides prompt written notice within 24 hours when prior notice is not practicable, and (iii) produces a post-incident access report documenting personnel, actions, and data accessed."

2) We will include SLA/controls language referencing role-based access, break-glass approvals, and IP allow-listing.

3) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and the evidence binder (redacted) can be provided under NDA. For legal hold / e-discovery we will describe the playbook and provide the contact for incident/legal escalation.

If Atlas agrees to the DR carve-out language above we will incorporate it into the next redline and return for a final pass.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP Legal (Enterprise Contracts)
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@atlas-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — snapshot/backups & cross-border access

Marissa / Sofia — thanks, that is much clearer. Atlas team is fine with the DR carve-out as long as two additional items make it into the DPA: (1) an explicit commitment that any non-US personnel engaged under the carve-out will be bound by equivalent contractual confidentiality and data handling obligations, and (2) a retention cap on archival backups unless Atlas signs off in writing for extensions.

Proposed short insertion for (1): "Any personnel engaged under the DR carve-out will be subject to contractual obligations at least as protective as those in this Agreement, including confidentiality, data minimization and restrictions on onward transfer."

We will also need a sample deletion ledger format to validate fields (timestamp, object id, snapshot id, operation, actor). If you can include a CSV example that would speed review.

Posting our legal hold/processing checklist to you now — see attached in a follow-up from legal@atlas-payments.com.

Regards,
Dan
Senior Counsel
Atlas Payments
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@atlas-payments.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — snapshot/backups & cross-border access

Dan / Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed insertions. Action items and next steps: 

- Marissa to produce a redline incorporating the DR carve-out and the non-US personnel contractual equivalence language; target: EOD Thu 2028-09-14.
- Ben & Aditya to produce a deletion ledger sample CSV and confirm the exact fields we will export; target: EOD Thu 2028-09-14.
- Sofia to provide SOC 2 Type II evidence under NDA and the internal playbook summary for legal hold processing; target: next business day after NDA execution.
- Tentative follow-up: 30-minute handshake call on Fri 2028-09-15 11:00 AM PT to close the remaining bullet points. I will send a calendar invite if that works for Atlas.

We will return a formal redline and the ledger example in the attachments referenced. Thanks again for working collaboratively on this — we want to make residency guarantees practical while preserving recoverability for customers.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head, Infosec Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (will attach updated redline and ledger CSV in follow-up)
